metadata.title: Marketplace Channel Integration Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: How EffectConnect must change when marketplaces, regulation, the Katapull group, pricing models or buying behaviour shift.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: One hand-built connector per marketplace and per webshop, prices and stock pushed in nightly batches, credentials stored with settings, and a single support team fixing failures reported by merchants.
metadata.residualArchitecture: A canonical offer, order and shipment model behind versioned marketplace adapters; shared job queue with rate-limit governance and an event log visible to merchants and consultants; rule-based content and pricing per channel; a partner-tenant model that lets other SaaS embed the hub; entitlements decoupled from metering so pricing models can change; and connectors to Katapull siblings treated as products.
metadata.note: Stressors marked candidate are plausible scenarios, not announced changes.

stressors.name: A major marketplace replaces its seller API
stressors.detection: Deprecation notices from bol or Amazon, partner programme briefings.
stressors.attractor: All adapters for that marketplace must be rebuilt before a hard cut-off while merchants keep selling.
stressors.businessReaction: Rebuild the adapter behind the canonical model and migrate connections in waves.
stressors.residue: Versioned adapters behind a stable canonical model; merchants and partners never integrate marketplace APIs directly.

impacts.effect: Adapter versions behind the canonical model.
Share of marketplace API changes absorbed by the hub.

media.alt: Illustration of the residuality stressor 'A major marketplace replaces its seller API', showing its signal, attractor, business response, and surviving residue.

stressors.name: A back-office vendor drops its own marketplace connector
stressors.detection: Back-office partner announces end of its own bol integration; inbound demand from its merchants.
stressors.attractor: Many merchants must switch integrator within months.
stressors.businessReaction: Offer a migration playbook and native connector from the back office, with onboarding capacity planned for the wave.
stressors.residue: Back-office connectors as first-class products and a repeatable migration path, built on the canonical model and versioned adapters.

impacts.effect: Native Logic4 connector absorbs the migrating merchants.
Time to go live becomes the competitive weapon.

stressors.name: Regulation demands more product data on marketplaces
stressors.detection: Marketplaces add mandatory attributes (e.g. manufacturer and responsible-person data under EU product safety rules) and reject listings without them.
stressors.attractor: Listings are blocked until new attributes are filled across the assortment.
stressors.businessReaction: Add the attributes to category schemas, rules to derive them and bulk validation.
stressors.residue: Schema refresh and validation that make new mandatory attributes visible before listings fail.

media.alt: Illustration of the residuality stressor 'Regulation demands more product data on marketplaces', showing its signal, attractor, business response, and surviving residue.

stressors.name: Katapull adds a WMS (Picqer) to the Commerce Hub
stressors.detection: Katapull announced the Picqer acquisition on 7 October 2026.
stressors.attractor: Merchants expect marketplace orders, stock and LVB replenishment to flow natively between hub brands.
stressors.businessReaction: Use Embedded Integrations and the back-office connector contract for Picqer, DeliveryMatch and Returnista.
stressors.residue: A partner-tenant model and uniform order format reused by every sibling.

impacts.effect: Sibling WMS and shipping brands embed marketplace connections.

media.title: Residuality stressor illustration: Katapull adds a WMS (Picqer) to the Commerce Hub
media.alt: Illustration of the residuality stressor 'Katapull adds a WMS (Picqer) to the Commerce Hub', showing its signal, attractor, business response, and surviving residue.

stressors.name: Competitors switch to aggressive fixed or free entry pricing
stressors.detection: Competitor price pages and lost deals cite free plugins or lower entry tiers.
stressors.attractor: Fixed-fee differentiation weakens at the low end.
stressors.businessReaction: Change plan packaging without code changes and compete on service and Katapull integration.
stressors.residue: Entitlements and metering decoupled from features so pricing can change quickly.

media.title: Residuality stressor illustration: Competitors switch to aggressive fixed or free entry pricing
media.alt: Illustration of the residuality stressor 'Competitors switch to aggressive fixed or free entry pricing', showing its signal, attractor, business response, and surviving residue.

stressors.name: AI shopping agents become a meaningful sales channel
stressors.detection: Marketplaces and search platforms open agent-facing product and checkout APIs.
stressors.attractor: Content and offers must be machine-readable and current in new channels.
stressors.businessReaction: Treat agent channels as further adapters and feeds from the same catalogue and price rules.
stressors.residue: Canonical catalogue and offer model reused for any new channel type.
